speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I would assume that there would be declarations made by the company and penalties attached to false declarations.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, is it generally going by declarations made or is there further verification that is attempted to be done by the agencies?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Can some of the burden of checking be handled by auditors?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: One assumes the auditors do, actually, based on sample checks, check compliance with the Government's incentives, but they may not do so in all cases, I am supposing.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, is there more that can be done to require the auditors to flag out cases of non-compliance so that some of that burden of checking is outsourced, as it were?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: There is a spectrum of ways in which verification, as the Member put it, can be done.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This starts from declaration by the companies, obviously.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But it also extends to the checks done by our agencies and also, in some cases, there is feedback that is received and they act upon that.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, materiality of the issue should be taken into account.
